name: s86-stop-gate-no-python-per-file-state-fail-closed
setup_commands: mkdir -p minbin && for t in bash sh git dirname basename tr date mkdir tail head sed grep cat env rm mv cp perl sleep cksum; do p=$(command -v "$t") && ln -sf "$p" "minbin/$t"; done; true
notes: A per-file state written while python3 worked, read at a stop without it. It can't be evaluated, so the session it holds records for is blocked with instructions — never read as clean — while a later session with no records in it is not.
